name: query
description:
Execute a structured JSON query against Affinity data. Supports filtering, includes, expands, aggregates, and multiple output formats.

📖 FIRST: Read xaffinity://query-guide for performance tips (especially field selection and expand limits).

⚠️ EXPAND/INCLUDE WARNING: These cause N+1 API calls (one per record).
- ALWAYS use dryRun=true FIRST to see estimated API calls before running
- 100 records with expand = ~100 API calls = ~2-3 minutes
- 400+ records may hit the 10-minute timeout ceiling
- See data-model resource for practical limits table

Query structure:
- from: Entity type ('persons', 'companies', 'opportunities', 'listEntries', 'interactions', 'notes')
- where: Filter conditions with operators (eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, contains, starts_with, starts_word, in, between, is_null, is_not_null, has_any, has_all, contains_any, contains_all)
- include: Related entities to fetch (e.g., ['companies', 'opportunities'] for persons; ['persons', 'companies', 'opportunities', 'interactions'] for listEntries)
- expand: Computed data to add to records (e.g., ['interactionDates'], ['unreplied']). Unlike include, expand merges data directly into each record.
- select: Fields to return (default: all). Use 'fields.*' for all custom fields on listEntries
- orderBy: Sort results [{field, direction}]. When every key is a sortable field (fields.<name>, up to 5, no groupBy/aggregate), Affinity sorts: empty values last, ties by id, ranked dropdowns by rank
- groupBy: Group by field for aggregates (e.g., 'fields.Status' for listEntries)
- aggregate: Compute aggregates {alias: {sum/avg/count/min/max: field}}
- limit: Max records to return

Advanced filtering (quantifiers, exists, count):
- all: All related items must match condition - {"all": {"path": "companies", "where": {"path": "name", "op": "contains", "value": "Inc"}}}
- none: No related items may match condition - {"none": {"path": "interactions", "where": {"path": "type", "op": "eq", "value": "spam"}}}
- exists: At least one related item exists - {"exists": {"from": "interactions"}} or with filter {"exists": {"from": "interactions", "where": {"path": "type", "op": "eq", "value": "email"}}}
- _count: Count of related items - {"path": "companies._count", "op": "gte", "value": 2}
- Note: Nested quantifiers (all/none/exists inside each other) are not supported

Multi-select field filtering:
- eq with scalar value: checks if value is in the array (membership)
- eq with array value: checks set equality (order-insensitive)
- has_any: checks if array contains any of the specified values
- has_all: checks if array contains all of the specified values
- contains_any: any array element contains any substring (case-insensitive)
- contains_all: array elements collectively contain all substrings (case-insensitive)

Matching rules:
- starts_word: a word in the value starts with the text, case-insensitive, as Affinity's search matches names ("Jan" matches "Jane Doe" and "Mary-Jane"; "ane" doesn't)
- Person and company field values are compared by name ("Jane Doe", "Acme"). contains/contains_any/contains_all on them is refused: use starts_word
- An empty multi-value field counts as empty: is_null matches it, is_not_null doesn't

Filtering on Affinity's side:
- Conditions on fields (fields.<name>) that Affinity's search can answer are sent to Affinity, so only matching records are downloaded. The full where still runs locally on what comes back: results are the same as a local filter
- Stays local: all/none/exists/_count, non-field paths (entityName, createdAt, ...), expr, contains_any/contains_all, an OR with a branch Affinity can't answer
- companies/persons: a where must include at least one condition on their fields (fields.<name>); the rest (e.g. name contains) runs on what comes back. A where with no field condition is refused (it would read Affinity's whole company directory); for name/email search use execute-read-command with 'company ls --query TERM' / 'person ls --query TERM'. opportunities take no where
- When two list fields share a name, fields.<name> is refused with the ids: use fields.<field id> (any field can be named by id)

listEntries queries:
- Require 'listId' or 'listName' filter (listName resolves to ID at runtime)
- Custom field values are auto-fetched when referenced in groupBy, aggregate, or where
- Use 'fields.<FieldName>' (or 'fields.<field id>') paths for list fields
- Select fields: listEntryId, entityId, entityName, entityType, listId, createdAt, fields.<Name>, fields.*

Examples:
- {"from": "companies", "where": {"and": [{"path": "fields.Industry", "op": "eq", "value": "Software"}, {"path": "name", "op": "contains", "value": "Labs"}]}, "limit": 50}
- {"from": "listEntries", "where": {"path": "listName", "op": "eq", "value": "Dealflow"}, "select": ["listEntryId", "entityName", "fields.Status"]}
- {"from": "listEntries", "where": {"and": [{"path": "listName", "op": "eq", "value": "Dealflow"}, {"path": "entityName", "op": "contains", "value": "Acme"}]}}
- {"from": "opportunities", "include": ["companies"], "orderBy": [{"field": "created_at", "direction": "desc"}]}
- {"from": "listEntries", "where": {"and": [{"path": "listName", "op": "eq", "value": "Dealflow"}, {"path": "fields.Owner", "op": "starts_word", "value": "Jan"}]}, "orderBy": [{"field": "fields.Deal Size", "direction": "desc"}], "limit": 20}
- {"from": "listEntries", "where": {"and": [{"path": "listName", "op": "eq", "value": "Dealflow"}, {"path": "persons._count", "op": "gte", "value": 2}]}, "limit": 100}
- {"from": "persons", "where": {"and": [{"path": "fields.Seniority", "op": "eq", "value": "Executive"}, {"exists": {"from": "interactions"}}]}, "limit": 50}
- {"from": "listEntries", "where": {"path": "listName", "op": "eq", "value": "Dealflow"}, "expand": ["interactionDates"], "limit": 50}
- {"from": "listEntries", "where": {"path": "listName", "op": "eq", "value": "Dealflow"}, "include": ["persons", "companies"], "limit": 50}
- {"from": "listEntries", "where": {"path": "listName", "op": "eq", "value": "Dealflow"}, "expand": ["unreplied"], "limit": 50}

Performance notes:
- Includes cause N+1 API calls (1 per parent record) - use dryRun to preview
- Expand (interactionDates) also causes N+1 API calls (1 per record)
- Quantifiers (all, none, exists) and _count also cause N+1 API calls to fetch relationship data
- Quantifier queries on 'persons' or 'companies' make requests per matching record: keep the field condition narrow and maxRecords low (1000 records can take 20+ minutes)\n- Recommended: Start from 'listEntries' (bounded by list) instead of unbounded entities for quantifier queries\n- Use dryRun=true to preview the execution plan with estimated API calls before running
- PRACTICAL LIMITS: expand/include queries support up to ~400 records via MCP (10-min ceiling). For larger exports, batch queries or use CLI directly.

For complete query language reference (all operators, aggregations, advanced filtering), read the xaffinity://query-guide resource.

query.description: JSON query object with 'from' (required) and optional where, include, expand, select, orderBy, groupBy, aggregate, having, limit fields.

where.description: Filter conditions. Simple: {path, op, value}. Compound: {and: [...]} or {or: [...]}

expand.description: Computed data to add to records. Available: 'interactionDates' (last/next meeting, email dates, team members), 'unreplied' (detect unreplied incoming messages - email/chat). Unlike include, expand merges data into each record.

select.description: Fields to return (default: all). Note: Expansions (from 'expand') are automatically included in output even when select is specified.

groupBy.description: Field to group by for aggregates

dryRun.description: If true, return the execution plan with estimated API calls without running the query.

maxRecords.description: Safety limit for maximum records to fetch (default 1000, max 10000). Note: MCP gateway enforces the same limits on CLI pagination commands via the execute-read-command tool.

timeout.description: Query timeout in seconds. If not specified (0 or omitted), timeout is auto-calculated based on estimated API calls (~2s per call, minimum 30s). Specify explicitly to override.

maxOutputBytes.description: Maximum output size in bytes (default 50000). Larger outputs are truncated.

format.description: Output format (applies to query results only; ignored when dryRun=true which always returns JSON execution plan). Options: 'toon' (default, 40% fewer tokens for large results), 'markdown' (best for analysis/summarization), 'json' (full envelope with pagination/includes), 'csv'/'jsonl' (for export/downstream processing)

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from previous truncated response. Pass the exact 'nextCursor' value to resume fetching. The query object AND format parameter must be IDENTICAL to the original request. Cursors expire after 1 hour. Works with all formats (toon, markdown, json, jsonl, csv). NEVER fabricate a cursor; it contains cryptographic hashes and will fail validation.

timeoutHint: Use dryRun=true to test filters first. For large datasets, set limit <= 100 and avoid expand/include.
